name: Academy Awards
hook: The statue, the first banquet and the record-holders: the Oscar questions Jeopardy asks most.

facts.label: the first ceremony
facts.statement: The first Academy Awards were a private banquet on May 16, 1929, in the Blossom Room of Hollywood's Roosevelt Hotel — and were not televised.

facts.label: the Oscar statuette
facts.statement: Los Angeles artist George Stanley sculpted the Oscar statuette, first handed out at the 1929 banquet.

facts.label: Bob Hope
facts.statement: Bob Hope first hosted in 1940 and joked in 1968, "Welcome to the Academy Awards, or, as it's known at my house, Passover."

facts.label: Katharine Hepburn
facts.statement: Katharine Hepburn won four Best Actress Oscars; her 48-year span between wins, 1933 to 1981, is the longest for a performer.

facts.label: Meryl Streep
facts.statement: Meryl Streep earned Oscar nominations in all but four years from 1979 to 1991, starting with The Deer Hunter.

facts.label: Halle Berry
facts.statement: Halle Berry became the first African-American woman to win Best Actress, for Monster's Ball.

facts.label: Whoopi Goldberg
facts.statement: Whoopi Goldberg won a supporting Oscar for Ghost and has also won a Grammy, Emmy and Tony.
